summary: Built the scoring and matched-budget measurement harness and repointed it three times as the spec changed (binary-claim market -> Scope Desk verdict evaluation -> Lean four-arm sharing evaluation). It scores nothing real yet: no frozen key, answers, ledger or Lean records exist in this checkout. Every number it prints must come from files other owners write. All hand-computed expectations and all simulated power fixtures live in tests only.
delivered: market/desk.py + prereg_desk.json: Scope Desk scoring. False-alarm rate on applies items first; false reassurance; accuracy; 3-class Brier; log loss; diagnosis exactness; oracle-supplied repair success; applies-vs-not calibration, AUC and operating curve; proved/simulated/descriptive rows kept separate; TXT textbook-criterion arm; arms compared only at matched tokens (<=5% of the smaller arm); family-cluster bootstrap; exact McNemar; INSUFFICIENT FAMILIES below 6 families; key sha256 and excluded-source-claim guards.

market/lean.py + prereg_lean.json: theorem coverage at matched compiler calls for L0 deterministic tactics, L1 sequential agent with persistent library, L2 private libraries, L3 shared library. Sharing supported only if L3 beats both L2 and L1; direct-reuse diagnostic states when a gain is not attributed to reuse.
market/basin.py: held-out Beta-Binomial scoring of basin-volume probabilities; Lean-clamped nodes that still pattern are counted as re-indexed, never averaged.

market/diversity.py: crowd error = mean individual error - diversity, checked numerically on every call (raises above 1e-12). Demoted to an appendix per the director; carries the theorem-limit text (guarantees only vs the MEAN individual, says nothing about the BEST).

market/scoring.py, aggregate.py (mean, median, log-opinion pool, fixed extremisation a=1.5, out-of-fold recalibration), calibration.py (bins, ECE, reliability figure, family error correlation, within-outcome variant), stats.py (Clopper-Pearson, McNemar, AUC, cluster bootstrap), arms.py (budget gate).
market/store.py + report.py: retained immutable hash-chained binary-claim forecast store and report from the first design; tested; NOT on the Scope Desk path. No separate market API was built.

market/triage.py: scorecard tally built on the frozen bench-v1-freeze.json (read from /data/worktrees/admissible-seed, not modified). Uses the freeze's own ids, buckets B0-B3 and verdict vocabulary; a verdict stands only with compiled artifact, clean axioms, non-author statement review, all mutants failing (proofs), scope condition or counterexample as relevant, and the mandatory B1 anti-triviality mutant; otherwise CLAIMED_BUT_UNVERIFIED. B0 claims cannot get verdicts; frozen buckets cannot change; no record counts as NOT_ATTEMPTED. The parser reads the real freeze (counts 2/4/11/4).

market/gate.py + prereg_gate.json: gate-vs-model-judgement evaluation (conditions U/G across model families). Trap error, refusal, false refusal, non-trap error, descriptive useful-correct; trivial policies (always-refuse shown to have zero trap error and total false refusal); paired G-vs-U family-cluster comparison; support rule requires fewer trap errors AND no detectable rise in false refusals or non-trap errors; token ratio reported not gated (precondition check, not a compute-matched collective test); circularity of the key and the gate stated in every report.

limitations: No real data has been scored. There is no measured finding in this file.

Input formats are my reading of scopedesk/SPEC.md (answers, key) plus ASSUMPTIONS for the arms ledger rows (arm plus total_tokens or token fields) and the Lean result rows (proved, axioms_clean, compiler_calls, optional cross_family_lemma_uses). I read the spec through git show and did not look at the owners' code. Confirm with the arms and bench owners.
The key is trusted: this harness cannot detect a wrong key. The independent key audit (AT3) is someone else's.

Cluster bootstrap needs enough independent families; with the few families a first catalogue may have, the harness reports INSUFFICIENT FAMILIES instead of a verdict. That is intended but may mean most comparisons are not decidable.
Within-arm dependence in the shared-library arm (statements share lemmas by design) is not modelled; pairing is across arms by statement.

The closest published replication of the shared-library mechanism (Berlot-Attwell et al., arXiv 2504.03048, as relayed in the host's post-audit) was negative after compute adjustment. A null is the prior-informed expectation and the harness is built to print it plainly. I relied on the host's relay of that paper and did not read it.
The binary-claim forecast store is an honest-process ledger, not protection against an adversary with file access.
Prereg files are committed before any agent answer exists but the hash binding to a run is only as good as the runner recording the report's prereg sha256.

Not done, deliberately: tournament/debate ranking (target repo unknown, cannot rule out duplication), any nanopub code (the Ashley-maintained skill exists and I wrote none), Kavita's seven-point claim spec, dataset discovery at scale, and any PR or outreach. Those are other roles' work or need the user's authorization.
The triage tally trusts the records it is given; it cannot check that a Lean artifact compiles or that a mutant set is meaningful. Those checks belong to the proof owners and the independent audit.

Gate evaluation: the trap key and the gate share exact linear arithmetic, so G's trap error of 0 is a consistency check, not independent validation. Trap truth is the LINEAR statement (no admissible mode in the band); a nonlinear pattern can still form. Independent evidence is the Lean certificate and, for nonlinear outcomes, two-solver agreement.

Not done, deliberately: the turing-scope-check package and MCP server, the robustness-curve figure against measured morphogen diffusivities, and the item generator for the trap questions. Those belong to the gate and bench owners; the harness only scores their outputs.
